description: Full collection-config control for Weaviate Cloud, plus schema history, drift diffing, and lint that no other Weaviate tool has.

tools.name: indexes_get
tools.description: Returns per-property index state including active reindex progress. This powers the UI to show live migration status. Required: className.

params.name: className
params.description: Class name

tools.name: properties_add
tools.description: Adds a new property definition to an existing collection (`className`) definition. Required: className. Optional: bucketGeneration, dataType, description (plus 11 more). Returns the new Property.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) to add the property to.

params.name: bucketGeneration
params.description: Internal RAFT-replicated counter bumped by semantic runtime-reindex migrations (e.g. change-tokenization, enable-filterable, enable-searchable). Used by the data path to resolve the property's inverted-index bucket name; a single RAFT commit flipping the schema flag AND bumping this counter atomically cuts the cluster from the old bucket to the new one. Defaults to 0. Internal use; clients should not set this.

params.name: dataType
params.description: Data type of the property (required). If it starts with a capital (for example Person), may be a reference to another type.

params.name: description
params.description: Description of the property.

params.name: disableDuplicatedReferences
params.description: If set to false, allows multiple references to the same target object within this property. Setting it to true will enforce uniqueness of references within this property. By default, this is set to true.

params.name: indexFilterable
params.description: Whether to include this property in the filterable, Roaring Bitmap index. If `false`, this property cannot be used in `where` filters. Note: Unrelated to vectorization behavior.

params.name: indexInverted
params.description: (Deprecated). Whether to include this property in the inverted index. If `false`, this property cannot be used in `where` filters, `bm25` or `hybrid` search. Unrelated to vectorization behavior (deprecated as of v1.19; use indexFilterable or/and indexSearchable instead)

params.name: indexRangeFilters
params.description: Whether to include this property in the filterable, range-based Roaring Bitmap index. Provides better performance for range queries compared to filterable index in large datasets. Applicable only to properties of data type int, number, date.

params.name: indexSearchable
params.description: Optional. Should this property be indexed in the inverted index. Defaults to true. Applicable only to properties of data type text and text[]. If you choose false, you will not be able to use this property in bm25 or hybrid search. This property has no affect on vectorization decisions done by modules

params.name: moduleConfig
params.description: Configuration specific to modules in a collection context.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the property (required). Multiple words should be concatenated in camelCase, e.g. `nameOfAuthor`.

params.name: nestedProperties
params.description: The properties of the nested object(s). Applies to object and object[] data types.

params.name: searchableBlockmax
params.description: Internal RAFT-replicated per-property flag: true iff this property's searchable (BM25) bucket is on the blockmax (StrategyInverted) index. Stamped at migration cutover. Absent/null means 'not stamped' and is resolved against the class-wide UsingBlockMaxWAND flag. Internal use; clients must not set this.

params.name: text-analyzer-ascii-fold
params.description: If true, accent/diacritic marks are folded to their base characters during indexing and search. For example, 'Ã©cole' matches 'ecole'. Defaults to false.

params.name: text-analyzer-ascii-fold-ignore
params.description: If provided, specifies a list of characters that should be excluded from ascii folding. For example, if ['Ã©'] is provided, then 'Ã©' will not be folded to 'e' during indexing and search. This list is immutable after the property is created.

params.name: text-analyzer-stopword-preset
params.description: Stopword preset name. Overrides the collection-level invertedIndexConfig.stopwords for this property. Only applies to properties using 'word' tokenization. Can be a built-in preset ('en', 'none') or a user-defined preset from invertedIndexConfig.stopwordPresets.

params.name: tokenization
params.description: Determines how a property is indexed. This setting applies to `text` and `text[]` data types. The following tokenization methods are available: - `word` (default): Splits the text on any non-alphanumeric characters and lowercases the tokens. - `lowercase`: Splits the text on whitespace and lowercases the tokens. - `whitespace`: Splits the text on whitespace. This tokenization is case-sensitive. - `field`: Indexes the entire property value as a single token after trimming whitespace. - `trigram`: Splits the property into rolling trigrams (three-character sequences). - `gse`: Uses the `gse` tokenizer, suitable for Chinese language text. [See `gse` docs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-ego/gse#section-readme). - `kagome_ja`: Uses the `Kagome` tokenizer with a Japanese (IPA) dictionary. [See `kagome` docs](https://github.com/ikawaha/kagome). - `kagome_kr`: Uses the `Kagome` tokenizer with a Korean dictionary. [See `kagome` docs](https://github.com/ikawaha/kagome). See [Reference: Tokenization](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/collections#tokenization) for details.

tools.name: properties_index_cancel
tools.description: Cancels the in-flight reindex task targeting this property's index. No request body. Idempotent: succeeds whether or not a task was in flight (a `202` with `{'status':'NO_OP'}` is returned when there is nothing to cancel). `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`. Required: className, propertyName, indexName (default: filterable). Returns the new IndexUpdateResponse.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

params.name: propertyName
params.description: The name of the property whose reindex task should be cancelled.

params.name: indexName
params.description: The inverted index type whose in-flight task should be cancelled. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

tools.name: properties_index_objects-properties-delete
tools.description: Deletes an inverted index of a specific property within a collection (`className`). The index to delete is identified by `indexName` and must be one of `filterable`, `searchable`, or `rangeFilters` (with `rangeable` accepted as an alias for `rangeFilters`). Required: className, propertyName, indexName (default: filterable). Destructive.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

params.name: propertyName
params.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be deleted.

params.name: indexName
params.description: The name of the inverted index to delete from the property. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

tools.name: properties_index_rebuild
tools.description: Rebuilds the inverted index from the stored objects with its current configuration (repair / format refresh). No request body. Index-mutating work is asynchronous: a `202` with a task ID is returned. `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`. Required: className, propertyName, indexName (default: filterable). Optional: tenants. Returns the new IndexUpdateResponse.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

params.name: propertyName
params.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be rebuilt.

params.name: indexName
params.description: The inverted index type to rebuild. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

params.name: tenants
params.description: Tenant names to target. Allowed for all index types on multi-tenant collections (rebuilds are format-only). Omit to target all tenants.

tools.name: properties_index_upsert
tools.description: Upserts the inverted index of a property, identified by `indexName`. The body describes the desired index configuration; the server diffs it against the current state and either creates the index, migrates its configuration, or does nothing. Index-mutating work is asynchronous: a `202` with a task ID is returned when a reindex task is submitted, and `200` with `{'status':'NO_OP'}` is returned when the desired configuration is already in place. `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`. Required: className, propertyName, indexName (default: filterable). Optional: tenants, algorithm, tokenization. Returns the updated IndexUpdateResponse.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

params.name: propertyName
params.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be upserted.

params.name: indexName
params.description: The inverted index type to upsert. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

params.name: tenants
params.description: Tenant names to target. Only valid on multi-tenant collections and only when the resulting operation is format-only (on PUT that is `rangeFilters` creation). Omit to target all tenants.

params.name: algorithm
params.description: Target BM25 algorithm for a `searchable` index. Only `blockmax` is a valid target (input aliases `block-max`, `block_max`, `blockmaxwand`, `bmw` are accepted case-insensitively). From WAND this triggers the Map â†’ BlockMax migration; on an already-`blockmax` index it is a NO_OP. `wand` is rejected (deprecated); downgrade is intentionally not supported.

params.name: tokenization
params.description: Target tokenization for a `searchable` or `filterable` index. Required when creating a `searchable` index; optional otherwise (omitted = keep the current value). On `filterable` creation it must be omitted or equal the property's current tokenization.

tools.name: properties_tokenize_objects-properties
tools.description: Tokenizes the provided text using the tokenization method configured for the specified property. This endpoint automatically applies the property's tokenization setting and the collection's stopword configuration, making it useful for understanding exactly how text will be processed for a given property during indexing and querying. Required: className, propertyName, text. Returns the new TokenizeResponse.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

params.name: propertyName
params.description: The name of the property whose tokenization configuration should be used.

params.name: text
params.description: The text to tokenize using the property's configured tokenization.

tools.name: schema_dump
tools.description: Retrieves the definitions of all collections (classes) currently in the database schema. Returns array of Class.

tools.name: schema_objects-create
tools.description: Defines and creates a new collection (class). If [`AutoSchema`](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/collections#auto-schema) is enabled (not recommended for production), Weaviate might attempt to infer schema from data during import. Manual definition via this endpoint provides explicit control. Optional: class, description, invertedIndexConfig (plus 10 more). Returns array of Property.

params.name: class
params.description: Name of the collection (formerly 'class') (required). Multiple words should be concatenated in CamelCase, e.g. `ArticleAuthor`.

params.name: description
params.description: Description of the collection for metadata purposes.

params.name: inverted-index-config-bm25-b
params.description: Calibrates term-weight scaling based on the document length (default: 0.75).

params.name: inverted-index-config-bm25-k1
params.description: Calibrates term-weight scaling based on the term frequency within a document (default: 1.2).

params.name: inverted-index-config-cleanup-interval-seconds
params.description: Asynchronous index clean up happens every n seconds (default: 60).

params.name: inverted-index-config-index-null-state
params.description: Index each object with the null state (default: `false`).

params.name: inverted-index-config-index-property-length
params.description: Index length of properties (default: `false`).

params.name: inverted-index-config-index-timestamps
params.description: Index each object by its internal timestamps (default: `false`).

params.name: inverted-index-config-stopword-presets
params.description: User-defined named stopword lists. Each key is a preset name that can be referenced by a property's textAnalyzer.stopwordPreset field. The value is an array of stopword strings. Preset names must not be empty or whitespace-only; each list must contain at least one word; individual words must not be empty or whitespace-only.

params.name: inverted-index-config-stopwords-additions
params.description: Stopwords to be considered additionally (default: []). Can be any array of custom strings.

params.name: inverted-index-config-stopwords-preset
params.description: Pre-existing list of common words by language (default: `en`). Options: [`en`, `none`].

params.name: inverted-index-config-stopwords-removals
params.description: Stopwords to be removed from consideration (default: []). Can be any array of custom strings.

params.name: inverted-index-config-tokenizer-user-dict
params.description: User-defined dictionary for tokenization.

params.name: inverted-index-config-using-block-max-wand
params.description: Using BlockMax WAND for query execution (default: `false`, will be `true` for new collections created after 1.30).

params.name: moduleConfig
params.description: Configuration specific to modules in a collection context.

params.name: multiTenancyConfig
params.description: Configuration related to multi-tenancy within a collection (class)

params.name: objectTtlConfig
params.description: Configuration of objects' time-to-live

params.name: properties
params.description: Define properties of the collection.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-diff-batch-size
params.description: Maximum number of object keys included in a single diff batch.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-diff-per-node-timeout
params.description: Timeout in seconds for computing a diff against a single node.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-frequency
params.description: Base frequency in milliseconds at which async replication runs diff calculations.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-frequency-while-propagating
params.description: Frequency in milliseconds at which async replication runs while propagation is active.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-hashtree-height
params.description: Height of the hashtree used for diffing.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-logging-frequency
params.description: Interval in seconds at which async replication logs its status.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-pre-propagation-timeout
params.description: Overall timeout in seconds for the pre-propagation phase.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-propagation-batch-size
params.description: Number of objects to include in a single propagation batch.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-propagation-concurrency
params.description: Maximum number of concurrent propagation workers.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-propagation-delay
params.description: Delay in milliseconds before newly added or updated objects are propagated.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-propagation-limit
params.description: Maximum number of objects to propagate in a single async replication run.

params.name: replication-config-async-config-propagation-timeout
params.description: Timeout in seconds for propagating batch of changes to a node.

params.name: replication-config-deletion-strategy
params.description: Conflict resolution strategy for deleted objects.

params.name: replication-config-factor
params.description: Number of times a collection (class) is replicated (default: 1).

params.name: shardingConfig
params.description: Manage how the index should be sharded and distributed in the cluster

params.name: vectorConfig
params.description: Configure named vectors. Either use this field or `vectorizer`, `vectorIndexType`, and `vectorIndexConfig` fields. Available from `v1.24.0`.

params.name: vectorIndexConfig
params.description: Vector-index config, that is specific to the type of index selected in vectorIndexType

params.name: vectorIndexType
params.description: Name of the vector index type to use for the collection (e.g. `hnsw` or `flat`).

params.name: vectorizer
params.description: Specify how the vectors for this collection should be determined. The options are either `none` - this means you have to import a vector with each object yourself - or the name of a module that provides vectorization capabilities, such as `text2vec-weaviate`. If left empty, it will use the globally configured default ([`DEFAULT_VECTORIZER_MODULE`](https://docs.weaviate.io/deploy/configuration/env-vars)) which can itself either be `none` or a specific module.

tools.name: shards_get
tools.description: Retrieves the status of all shards associated with the specified collection (`className`). For multi-tenant collections, use the `tenant` query parameter to retrieve status for a specific tenant's shards. Required: className. Optional: tenant. Returns array of ShardStatusGetResponse.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) whose shards to query.

params.name: tenant
params.description: The name of the tenant for which to retrieve shard statuses (only applicable for multi-tenant collections).

tools.name: shards_update
tools.description: Updates the status of a specific shard within a collection (e.g., sets it to `READY` or `READONLY`). This is typically used after resolving an underlying issue (like disk space) that caused a shard to become non-operational. There is also a convenience function in each client to set the status of all shards of a collection. Required: className, shardName. Optional: status. Returns the updated ShardStatus.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the shard.

params.name: shardName
params.description: The name of the shard to update.

params.name: status
params.description: Status of the shard

tools.name: tenants_create
tools.description: Creates one or more new tenants for a specified collection (`className`). Multi-tenancy must be enabled for the collection via its definition. Required: className. Returns array of Tenant.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the multi-tenant enabled collection (class).

tools.name: tenants_delete
tools.description: Deletes one or more specified tenants from a collection (`className`). WARNING: This action permanently deletes all data associated with the specified tenants. Required: className. Destructive.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) from which to delete tenants.

tools.name: tenants_exists
tools.description: Checks for the existence of a specific tenant within the given collection (`className`). Required: className, tenantName.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) to check within.

params.name: tenantName
params.description: The name of the tenant to check for.

tools.name: tenants_get
tools.description: Retrieves a list of all tenants currently associated with the specified collection. Required: className. Returns array of Tenant.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) whose tenants to list.

tools.name: tenants_get-one
tools.description: Retrieves details about a specific tenant within the given collection (`className`), such as its current activity status. Required: className, tenantName. Returns the Tenant.

params.name: className
params.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the tenant.

params.name: tenantName
params.description: The name of the tenant to retrieve.

tools.name: tenants_update
tools.description: Updates the activity status (e.g., `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, etc.) of one or more specified tenants within a collection (`className`). Required: className. Returns array of Tenant.

params.name: className
